description: Reduce a strong-C1P weighted set-cover matrix to strictly monotone interval rows, then solve its column-node DAG by shortest path.

source.title: Set covering problems with consecutive ones property
source.reference: Preprint 2005-03, Institute of Numerical and Applied Mathematics, University of Göttingen
source.encyclopedia_entry: Michael Dom, Set Cover with Almost Consecutive Ones, Encyclopedia of Algorithms, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4_368
source.algorithm_attribution: Schöbel Algorithm 1 strict-monotone row reduction and Algorithm 2 shortest path on column intervals.

input.row_mask_rule: Bit j means column j covers the row; every nonzero row mask must have one contiguous run of 1-bits. A zero row is valid but uncoverable.

output.encoding: [minimum_total_weight], or [-1] for a valid uncoverable instance

workspace.meaning: Conservative fixed per-call budget for row interval endpoints, column interval endpoints, a ten-node shortest-path distance array, parser state, and staged output. The ten ports use fixed bounded arrays or equivalent bounded stack storage.

contract.precondition: Rows are already in strong C1P order: every row's 1-bits are consecutive in the supplied column order. Nonconsecutive masks are malformed.
contract.row_reduction: Sort nonempty rows by left endpoint. For equal left endpoints retain a shortest interval (duplicate intervals keep the earliest input row). Then retain only strict suffix minima of right endpoints, scanning from right to left; this implements Schöbel Algorithm 1's two row reductions with its rightmost tie rule.
contract.column_intervals: In the reduced row order, each nonempty column covers one contiguous interval of rows; empty columns are excluded from the DAG.
contract.dag: There is a source arc to each column interval starting at row 0, an arc j->k for j<k when start[k] <= end[j]+1, and an arc from each interval ending at the last reduced row to the sink.
contract.arc_cost: Source arcs cost zero. Every outgoing arc from column j, including its sink arc, costs weight[j], so a path cost is the total weight of its selected columns.
contract.ties: Only the optimum weight is emitted; path ties do not affect the result.
contract.error_results: Malformed dimensions, weights, masks, or non-strong-C1P rows return -1. A valid zero row emits [-1]. Null or undersized output returns -2 without writes.

oracle_method: The primary applies strict-monotone interval-row reduction and the Schöbel column-interval shortest-path DAG. The independent oracle enumerates all column subsets directly and checks row coverage.
